obligations.note: The new route POST /payees/{id}/reopen uses action 'manage_payees' which is listed in the privileged actions of controls/payments/access-policy.json, yet it is defined with mfa=False. The CI control test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa fails, confirming the violation. The cited exception EXC-0183 expired on 2026-09-13, well before the 2026-10-16 review time, so it provides no valid coverage.

The CI run on the final commit 331108bb shows 1 failure (test_privileged_routes_require_mfa), meaning the full test suite is not passing. The change touches routes.py, which is in the scope of MFA-1, and the registered control test for that obligation is failing, so CHG-4 is not satisfied.

Ticket CHG-24857 is approved by Grace Kim (change_manager) and its components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.service, payments.store) cover all four changed files per the component mapping.
A code_review approval from Mara Costa (change_approver for payments) is recorded for the exact head commit; she is not the author (Aisha Bello) and is on the same team, which is permitted.
There is only one commit in the change and the approval names that commit, so there are no later commits to invalidate the approval.

The change touches security_sensitive components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.store). A security_review approval from Kofi Mensah (security_reviewer) for the correct commit is present and the reviewer is not the author.

The new SQL in store.reopen_payee uses a fixed string with a ? parameter bound to payee_id; the CI control test test_sql_statements_are_parameterized passed, confirming no string-built SQL was introduced.

The new reopen_payee service method calls self._audit(actor, 'reopen_payee', f'payee:{payee_id}'), recording actor, action, target and time, consistent with the audit pattern used by all other state-changing operations in the file.

The only cited exception, EXC-0183 for MFA-1 / payments.routes, expired on 2026-09-13. The review time is 2026-10-16, so the exception is out of date and cannot cover the MFA-1 deviation. No other valid exception is in the register for this obligation and component.

ACR-0404 in the acceptance ledger covers apps/baseline-payments/payments/routes.py at commit e5bf646 for MFA-1. This change adds a new route to routes.py, a behavioural modification, so that evidence lapses. No new evidence of equivalent strength is provided for the updated routes table.

summary: The change introduces a new privileged HTTP route (POST /payees/{id}/reopen, action manage_payees) but marks it mfa=False, directly violating MFA-1 since manage_payees is in the privileged-actions list. The CI run confirms this with a failing control test. The exception that was intended to cover this (EXC-0183) expired over a month before the review date, so no valid exception exists. CHG-4 fails because the CI suite has an unaddressed failure on the final commit. LAP-1 is also violated because the MFA-1 evidence in the acceptance ledger covers the old routes.py and the behavioural change lapses it. The change must be rejected; the route needs mfa=True or a new, unexpired exception with a compensating control must be obtained before re-submission.
